title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Decoder architecture & efficient attention
lessons.conceptOverview: Draw the tensor shapes through one decoder block. Calculate cache bytes as 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × tokens × bytes per element.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A decoder predicts the next token under a causal mask. RoPE encodes relative position through rotations; RMSNorm rescales activations and SwiGLU gates feed-forward features. MQA shares one key/value head and GQA shares them within groups, reducing KV-cache memory. The cache stores previous keys and values during decoding.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: The KV cache stores only model weights. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: A decoder predicts the next token under a causal mask. RoPE encodes relative position through rotations; RMSNorm rescales activations and SwiGLU gates feed-forward features. MQA shares one key/value head and GQA shares them within groups, reducing KV-cache memory. The cache stores previous keys and values during decoding. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: The KV cache stores only model weights.
keyTakeaways: A decoder predicts the next token under a causal mask.

lessons.title: Lab: Pretraining, tokenization & scaling
lessons.conceptOverview: Create a tiny next-token dataset. Shift targets by one token, mask padding, and compare validation loss against a frequency baseline.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A tokenizer maps text into a vocabulary of token IDs. Pretraining minimizes next-token cross entropy over large text corpora. Deduplication, quality filtering and held-out contamination checks are part of the data pipeline. Compute/data scaling tradeoffs compare parameter count and training tokens under a fixed budget, rather than assuming larger is always better.

lessons.title: Lab: Post-training & model families
lessons.conceptOverview: Write a comparison matrix for two specific model releases. Separate documented facts from unverified claims, and evaluate both on the same held-out tasks.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: SFT learns from instruction-response examples. RLHF uses preference feedback, often through a reward model; DPO optimizes relative preference directly. MoE activates a subset of experts per token, so active compute differs from total parameter memory. Compare GPT, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek and Mistral using model cards for the specific release: architecture, context, license, modalities and evaluations vary.
